Law-2 story conformance is DEFERRED until the project is mapped; it is NOT closed. The findings below are graded against the repo's own declared spec (lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md) and the contract's own NatSpec, which are the only authoritative intent artifacts that exist at 0bb82d8.

invariantVerdicts.invariant: Antimatter must never expose a burn
invariantVerdicts.evidence: src/Antimatter.sol contains exactly one _burn call, at line 215 inside annihilateFrom. Supply-mutating entry points are mint (:179, onlyApprovedMinters, _mint only) and annihilateFrom (:201). No ERC20Burnable inheritance (:21 is ERC20, Ownable, ReentrancyGuard), no burn/burnFrom/clawback function, and transfer-to-address(0) is blocked by OpenZeppelin v5.6.1 ERC20._update (ERC20InvalidReceiver). rescueERC20 (:263) moves ERC20s out but cannot destroy antimatter. The rule's substance is satisfied; the defect is in its trip-wire, see FAITH-003.

invariantVerdicts.verdict: HOLDS for the stablecoin leg; PARTIALLY VERIFIED for the phUSD leg
invariantVerdicts.evidence: Effects-before-interactions: _spendAllowance/_burn at :214-215 precede every external call, and all interactions are in the same call frame so any revert unwinds the burn (tests :218-274 confirm four distinct revert paths leave nothing half-settled). findings.specText: "brought together with an equal quantity of a supported stablecoin it annihilates, and the pair is emitted as phUSD — twice the quantity, since both halves are redeemed."
findings.actualBehavior: Both clauses of the stated rationale are false. (a) 'both halves are redeemed': phUSD has no redemption path — the stable leg's phUSD is minted by PhusdStableMinter.mint against a real stablecoin deposit forwarded to a yield strategy, but the antimatter leg's phUSD is minted at src/Antimatter.sol:236 (_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)) with no asset entering the protocol for it; nothing is 'redeemed' on that half because antimatter is itself an unbacked staking reward minted freely at :179. (b) 'twice the quantity': the total is amount + mintedForStable (:239), where mintedForStable honours the stable minter's exchangeRate. The repo's own test test_annihilateHonoursMinterExchangeRate (test/Annihilation.t.sol:108-117) asserts 195 phUSD for 100 antimatter at a 0.95 rate — i.e. the header's headline arithmetic is contradicted by the project's own passing test.
findings.deviation: The contract's authoritative NatSpec justifies the unbacked antimatter-leg mint with a redemption symmetry that does not exist, and states a 2x output the code does not guarantee. Per the audit's standing rule, in-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority and a falsely-authoritative doc raises rather than lowers severity: an integrator reading :13-20 would conclude both phUSD legs are asset-backed. Filed as a spec-conformance (F-XX) finding; the economic impact of the unbacked mint itself is econ-scanner's to size and is NOT dampened by this entry.

findings.specText: "antimatter's entire value to a holder is that it annihilates into phUSD worth twice its quantity" (CLAUDE.md) and "this contract mints the phUSD for the antimatter half" (src/Antimatter.sol:188-189)
findings.specSource: lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md § 'Antimatter must never expose a burn' (Why paragraph); src/Antimatter.sol:183-196
findings.actualBehavior: The code is FAITHFUL to this intent — :236 mints exactly `amount` phUSD to the recipient for the antimatter half. The intent itself is the hazard: antimatter is minted for free by the owner and approved minters (:179, no cap, no backing), and every unit is a standing claim on 1e18 freshly-minted phUSD that no asset backs. phUSD's collateral ratio is diluted by the entire outstanding antimatter supply, and the dilution is realisable by any holder at will.
findings.deviation: Law-1 override on Law-2: the declared intent, faithfully implemented, mints an unbacked liability. Escalated as a spec-level (rather than implementation-level) security finding. Deduplicate against econ-scanner's finding on the same mint at :236 — econ owns the impact sizing; this entry exists so the spec-conformance report records that the behaviour is intended, not accidental, and that its written justification (FAITH-001) is false.

findings.specText: "no new entry point that reaches `_burn` except `annihilateFrom`" ... "`test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints` in `test/Annihilation.t.sol` is a trip-wire for this rule."
findings.specSource: lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md § 'Antimatter must never expose a burn'
findings.actualBehavior: The trip-wire probes a hardcoded four-signature guess list (test/Annihilation.t.sol:344-345): burn(uint256), burn(address,uint256), burnFrom(address,uint256), annihilate(address,uint256). It asserts those four selectors revert. It cannot detect what the rule actually prohibits — ANY new entry point reaching _burn — because a burn path under any other name (redeem, destroy, clawback, sacrifice, an annihilate overload with a different arity, or a burn reached via a new admin function) is simply not in the list and the test passes green. Two further gaps: the rule also names 'no `transfer` to `address(0)` path' and 'no owner-callable clawback', and neither is probed at all (the transfer-to-zero case happens to be closed by OpenZeppelin's _update, i.e. by the base class, not by anything this repo asserts). Encoding note: all four signatures are encoded with two arguments (`abi.encodeWithSignature(signatures[i], user, 1 ether)`), so the one-argument burn(uint256) probe passes trailing calldata that Solidity's decoder ignores — it would decode amount = uint256(uint160(user)) = 2827 wei rather than 1 ether. It would still catch a naive burn(uint256) (2827 wei burns successfully, ok == true), but only because the test's address literal happens to be a small non-zero number; the probe is not testing what it reads as testing.
findings.deviation: CLAUDE.md designates this test as the enforcement mechanism for a load-bearing invariant and instructs future authors not to weaken it. The test is a name-denylist, not an invariant check, so it gives false assurance against the general rule it is nominated to guard. A genuinely load-bearing trip-wire would assert over the property (e.g. totalSupply is non-decreasing across every non-annihilateFrom external call, exercised by fuzzed calldata) or over the source (a single _burn occurrence, inside annihilateFrom). The invariant itself HOLDS at 0bb82d8 — this is a guard-quality finding, not a live burn exposure.

findings.specText: "Burn before the external calls, verify by measured balances rather than assumption, and let anything unexpected revert."
findings.specSource: lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md § 'Annihilation settles whole or not at all'
findings.actualBehavior: The measured-balance discipline is applied in full to the stablecoin leg (:219 stableBefore, :230 strict != check) but only nominally to the phUSD leg: :232 measures the delta and :233 rejects only the exact value zero. Any non-zero quantity is accepted on trust, including one wildly below what the stable deposit should have produced. Concretely, if PhusdStableMinter's exchangeRate for the stable is low or is changed between transaction submission and execution, the holder's antimatter is irreversibly burned at full quantity (:215) while the stable half returns almost no phUSD, and the transaction succeeds. annihilateFrom exposes no minimum-output / slippage parameter and performs no comparison against toStableAmount-implied expectation, so 'anything unexpected' does not revert — only 'nothing at all' does.
findings.deviation: Partial implementation of the spec's stated verification discipline: measurement is used for residue detection but not for expectation checking, on the one leg where the burn has already become irreversible. This does not breach the whole-or-nothing invariant as enumerated (no rest state has antimatter burned with stable undeposited, and nothing is stranded), which is why it is filed Low rather than as an invariant violation. The exchange-rate source is the stable minter, which CLAUDE.md deliberately makes the single source of truth (:104-105), so rate-setting itself is Law-3 owner territory; the gap here is the absence of any caller-side guard against it.

notes: recipient == address(this) is not rejected (:203 rejects only address(0)). Both phUSD legs would then be minted and transferred to the Antimatter contract itself, recoverable only via rescueERC20 — which CLAUDE.md says is 'a backstop, not a licence'. Not filed as a finding: it is a caller input mistake (C4 known-invalid class) and does not create a partial settlement. Worth a one-line guard.

toStableAmount (:246-258) trusts the stable minter's REGISTERED decimals rather than the token's own decimals(). A mis-registration there desynchronises the two legs, but registration is the minter owner's obvious, single-step act on an external contract — Law-3 suppressed, recorded here only so a later scan does not re-derive it as novel.
